summary.title: Mean Mode Screaming: Mean--Variance Split Residuals for 1000-Layer Diffusion Transformers

details: Ultra-deep Post-Norm Diffusion Transformers can silently enter a mean-dominated collapse state where token representations homogenize and centered variation is suppressed; the abrupt entry event is named Mean Mode Screaming (MMS).

Mechanistic account: row-stochastic attention leaves pure-mean token states invariant while the centered component is governed by PAP and can be contractive; residual-writer gradients split exactly into a rank-1 mean-coherent term T·δ̄ȳᵀ and a centered term, with the mean term entering O(T) coherent accumulation once tokens/adjoints align; once values homogenize, attention-logit gradients are killed by the Softmax Jacobian null space, locking in the collapse.

MV-Split Residuals: replace the Post-Norm merge X+F with a token-subspace-routed merge X + β⊙(PF) + α⊙J(F−X), i.e., a separately gained centered residual update plus a leaky replacement of the trunk mean (mean path becomes a per-feature leaky integrator), so mean-coherent and centered components get independent gains in both forward and backward passes — unlike token-isotropic gates (LayerScale/ReZero) that shrink both together.

Deliberately minimal single-stream multimodal DiT: Post-Norm RMSNorm residual chain, no AdaLN or per-layer modulation, no cross-attention (image + text tokens concatenated), SwiGLU FFN, QK-Norm, 2D RoPE on image tokens, d_model=1024, 8 heads.
Rectified flow matching objective on FLUX.2 VAE latents with a frozen Qwen3-0.6B text encoder; no explicit timestep embedding.
Residual writers W_O and W_2 zero-initialized in main runs (identity start); a standard-init 128-layer control also run.

Matched 400-layer comparison (5.45B params, 8×H100): un-stabilized baseline at LR η and η/2, LayerScale controls (λ_init swept 1e-2…1e-5), MV-Split (α_init=0, β_init=1); AdamW, global batch 1024, grad clipping 1.0, μP-scaled LR 1.5625e-4, 1000-step warmup, up to 100k steps.
Separate 1000-layer MV-Split run (13.64B params, 16×H100, β_init≈1/√L=0.03): ImageNet pretraining then SFT+DPO on ~50k curated images, reported only as scale validation.
Evaluation: FID-50K and Inception Score on ImageNet 256×256 at 10k–50k step checkpoints (Euler, 25 NFE, CFG w=2.0); GenEval/DPG-Bench for the post-trained 1000L checkpoint as calibration.

Writer gradient mode decomposition G_mean=||T δ̄ȳᵀ||_F vs G_ctr; alignment amplification A=||∇W||²/Σ||δ_t||²||y_t||² with absolute-coherence proxy κ̂; per-layer mean/centered energy ratio ρ_T, attention centered contraction ||PAP||₂, row diversity, variance gain, token cosine similarity.
Step-level spike trace: global-norm trigger, per-family top-K gradient norms, per-rank loss/output-gradient and NaN/Inf exclusion audit.
Propositions: A μ(X)=μ(X) for row-stochastic A; c(AX)=PAPX with contraction bound.

Exact writer-gradient decomposition (cross terms vanish identically); alignment-amplification identity A−1=(T−1)κ under equal-magnitude proxy with PSD Rayleigh-quotient form and absolute-coherence upper bound.
Lemma: if all V_j equal, ∂L/∂S_i=0 via J_sm(a)1=0; writer gradients bypass this null space.
Formal contrast with LayerScale/ReZero showing non-equivalence (LayerScale leaves trunk mean coefficient at 1) and closed-form fused backward for MV-Split+RMSNorm.
Hard centering X←PX, attention reparameterizations (A−I, I−A, (1−λ)I+λA), token-local gated attention, global gradient clipping, and Muon all fail to prevent the mean-dominated collapse.
Attention-branch-only MV-Split on 1000 layers: spike relocates to the unprotected FFN branch.
Segment-wise projectors (image/text blocks) used in the multimodal implementation; shown to still apply leaky control to the global mean mode.

key_findings.finding: Ultra-deep DiT divergence is a mode-selective residual-subspace failure: a mean-coherent writer-gradient shock opens residual branches, drives a mean-dominated forward state, and extinguishes Q/K learning.
key_findings.evidence: In a 400-layer baseline trace, the global gradient-norm spike is concentrated in G_mean with no comparable rise in G_ctr; Q/K gradients drop about four orders of magnitude while W_O gradients stay nonzero; ρ_T explodes, deep attention stays contractive on the centered subspace, and token cosine similarity approaches one in deep layers. Step-level audits exclude per-rank data outliers, loss-weight jumps, and NaN/Inf parameters.

key_findings.finding: The predicted alignment-amplification law holds: the spike coincides with loss of signed cross-token cancellation at residual writers, pushing the rank-1 mean update toward its O(T) coherent regime.
key_findings.evidence: At t*=3400 on the T=256 image-token segment, active layers for both Attn_WO and FFN_W2 sit near the absolute-coherence saturation envelope of A−1=(T−1)κ̂, whereas pre-spike samples lie well below it; the largest active layers reach A−1≈167, i.e. ~13× writer-gradient norm amplification over the independent-token baseline.

key_findings.finding: MV-Split removes collapse events and, under a stability constraint, substantially outperforms token-isotropic LayerScale at 400 layers.
key_findings.evidence: 400L baseline at default LR diverges before the first checkpoint and at η/2 diverges after 20k steps; MV-Split reaches FID/IS 7.23/89.8 @10k, 3.64/139.9 @20k, 2.60/185.5 @50k versus LayerScale's 14.08/59.2, 6.50/96.6, 2.90/165.5, while tracking close to the baseline's pre-crash trajectory.

key_findings.finding: The gain is mode-selective control, not a smaller effective learning rate.
key_findings.evidence: Writer gradient mode decomposition shows LayerScale bounds G_mean only by also compressing G_ctr into a low band, whereas MV-Split keeps G_mean bounded while G_ctr stays in a higher stable band; post-clipping global gradient norms for MV-Split occupy a higher bounded band than LayerScale without baseline-style spikes. Global gradient clipping cannot help since it scales G_mu and G_c by the same factor.
